completed_projects.title: Fix the lying context-index validators; machine-compute line_count; add index-orphan gate
completed_projects.description:
Make the context-index validation layer tell the truth. From the agent-system review (specs/reviews/review-2026-07-29-agent-system.md, docs/context section): 104 of 164 deployed index entries have wrong line_count (58 beyond the validator's own 10% tolerance; whole extension blocks are round-number placeholders that were never measured), 14 deployed context files including the single largest context file (patterns/task-lock.md, 1103 lines) have NO index entry and are unreachable by any agent, and the validator that should catch the line counts reports 'Warnings: 0 / Validation PASSED' while 58 real warnings scroll past.

WHAT IS WRONG:
  1. validate-context-index.sh (~lines 96-115) pipes jq into 'while read', so the loop runs in a subshell and every WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS+1)) increment is discarded. Fix with process substitution or a temp-file count so the summary reflects reality (and decide whether >tolerance mismatches should be errors, not warnings).
  2. line_count is typed by hand in every index-entries.json and drifts freely; nothing recomputes it. Add a small generator (or a --fix mode on the validator) that rewrites line_count from wc -l across all extensions' index-entries.json, and wire it into the deploy path so counts can never rot again.
  3. No script diffs DEPLOYED CONTEXT FILES against INDEX ENTRIES — check-extension-docs.sh's check_context_orphans diffs manifest provides.context against disk, never disk against index. Add an index-orphan gate beside it. Then resolve the current orphans: index or consciously exclude the 11 core files (patterns/task-lock.md, standards/git-staging-scope.md, patterns/lit-stage4a-flow.md, guides/hard-mode-routing.md, etc.) and the literature/email/memory/nvim strays.
  4. While in the file: the index has no version/generated top-level stamp despite the schema offering them — emit one so staleness is detectable.

VERIFICATION BAR:
  - Running validate-context-index.sh against the current deployed index reports the true warning/error count (nonzero before the line_count regeneration, zero after).
  - A deliberately-orphaned scratch context file makes the new gate fail; removing it passes.
  - All line_count fields across agent-system/extensions/*/index-entries.json match wc -l exactly after the generator runs.

SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): edit agent-system/extensions/**, never .claude/**. DELIVERABLE RULE: no task numbers in deliverables outside specs/**.
completed_projects.completion_summary: Made the context-index validation layer report true error/warning counts, regenerated all 458 source-store line_count values to exact wc -l matches, converted the deploy-index merge from append-only to upsert semantics so corrections actually reach the deployed index, indexed the 14 previously unreachable context files, and added two new automated gates (source line_count accuracy and deployed-index-orphan detection) to check-extension-docs.sh with empirically verified negative tests.

completed_projects.title: Bootstrap the errors.json lane for real: one schema, validated append script, reconciled docs
completed_projects.description:
Make the error-tracking layer real. specs/errors.json DOES NOT EXIST in this repo, yet it is the documented backbone of /errors, error-handling rules, and several skills' failure paths — every reader guards with [ -f ] and silently degrades to a no-op, so the self-healing loop the system's docs describe never runs. Three mutually inconsistent schemas are documented: rules/error-handling.md (context{session_id,command,task,phase,checkpoint} + trajectory + recovery), commands/errors.md (~line 21: context{command,task,agent,file} + recurrence_count, no trajectory/recovery; and a second update-shape at ~line 186 adding fixed_date/fix_task documented nowhere else), and the actual writer prose in skill-planner/SKILL.md (~line 487: recovery + fix_status, no trajectory/recurrence_count). Only 7 fields appear in all three.

THE PROVEN PATTERN TO MIRROR: the sibling events.jsonl substrate has exactly what errors.json lacks — a formal draft-07 schema (context/schemas/events-schema.json), a validated append script (scripts/events-append.sh: jq -c -n construction, flock serialization), and one format doc.

WORK:
  1. Decide ONE errors schema (start from the field union; make context sub-fields a superset; keep fix_status enum and add the empirically-observed 'resolved' value or normalize it away). Write context/schemas/errors-schema.json.
  2. Write scripts/errors-append.sh mirroring events-append.sh (schema-validated, flock'd, single writer). Create specs/errors.json with a valid empty shape ({"errors": []} — pick object-with-array over bare array and document why).
  3. Rewrite the three conflicting doc blocks (rules/error-handling.md, both blocks in commands/errors.md, the skill error-path prose) to point at the schema file instead of restating fields.
  4. Convert the inline jq error-append blocks in skills to call errors-append.sh.

SUBSUMES (fold in, then treat those tasks as superseded): the intent of task 954 (extend errors with a source-store defect lane — add the lane as a schema field/enum value here) and task 955 (reconcile errors.json schema drift — this task IS that reconciliation, done once with a schema instead of prose). Both were marked abandoned in favor of this task; their descriptions contain additional verified defect inventories worth reading before planning.

UNBLOCKS: tasks 951, 952, 953 (defect discrimination/recording/surfacing) all presuppose a durable, schema-stable error store.

VERIFICATION BAR:
  - errors-append.sh appends a schema-valid record under concurrent invocation (flock test) and rejects an off-schema record loudly.
  - specs/errors.json exists, validates against the schema, and /errors runs end-to-end against it without silent degradation.
  - grep across agent-system/extensions/core for inline '.errors +=' jq writes returns zero hits outside errors-append.sh.

completed_projects.title: One deploy engine: idempotent manifest-driven load, wipe+regenerate, full-category verification
completed_projects.description:
Collapse the TWO independent deploy engines writing .claude/ into one, and make deploy idempotent and fully verified. This is the structural fix for the recurring deploy-propagation defect class; it SUBSUMES tasks 958 and 970 (both marked abandoned in favor of this task — read their descriptions first: they contain the empirical reproductions and the verification bars to preserve).

ROOT CAUSES ESTABLISHED BY THE REVIEW (specs/reviews/review-2026-07-29-agent-system.md, deploy-pipeline section; all verified with file:line evidence):
  1. Engine A (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/loader.lua + init.lua) is manifest-driven and handles subdirectory scripts correctly, but manager.load() HARD-ABORTS on already-loaded (init.lua ~line 252), so nothing propagates to an existing deploy except via destructive unload/reload.
  2. Engine B (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/claude/commands/picker/operations/sync.lua load_all_globally) — the deploy-headless.sh path — never calls any loader copy function, is core-only, and its allow-list post-filter (~lines 1001-1016) matches provides.scripts entries by TOP directory segment while the manifest declares full relative paths, so EVERY scripts/lib|lint|tests entry is silently dropped on both fresh and existing deploys. This corrects the mis-diagnosis recorded in rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md (~lines 145-149): it is not an already-loaded skip — engine B never runs copy_scripts for anyone.
  3. The interactive picker path that remediation docs tell users to run ('Load Core / Sync all') NO LONGER EXISTS: the is_load_all entry has consumers (picker/init.lua ~line 111) but no producer (entries.lua creates only is_help and is_reload_all).
  4. manager.regenerate (init.lua ~line 972) — the wipe+regenerate design — has ZERO callers, and has a correctness bug: it calls settings_backup.restore AFTER manager.load has merged settings fragments, so the restore overwrites the fresh merge and new hook registrations are lost (the exact gap the wipe exists to fix). settings_backup.restore also never clears its staging dir, so a stale .claude-settings-backup/ silently reverts settings on every subsequent regenerate.
  5. verify.lua verify_extension covers agents/skills/rules/context but has zero references to scripts, hooks, docs, templates, systemd, root_files — exactly the categories that break.
  6. Engine A's 11 near-identical copy_* functions diverge internally: symlink guard in only 2 of 11, preserve_perms inconsistent, return arity differs.

WORK:
  1. Keep engine A. Add a force/resync mode to manager.load that skips the already-loaded abort and re-runs the (idempotent, overwrite-safe) copy sequence.
  2. Rewire deploy-headless.sh to manager.regenerate or unload-all/load-all; retire sync.load_all_globally and the dead is_load_all branch. Expose a [Regenerate] picker entry and a --wipe flag on deploy-headless.sh: backup -> rm -rf .claude -> regenerate -> restore-as-merge-base -> re-apply settings fragments -> clear staging.
  3. Fix the regenerate settings ordering bug and the staging-dir leak; wire settings_backup.backup (currently zero callers).
  4. Give .syncprotect backup/restore semantics (snapshot protected paths before wipe, restore after) — it is currently overwrite-protection only, so a wipe would lose context/repo/project-overview.md.
  5. Collapse the 11 copy_* functions into one table-driven copier ({category, source_subdir, target_subdir, recursive, preserve_perms, install_once}) so the symlink guard and perms handling hold for every category by construction.
  6. Extend verify.lua to declared-vs-deployed parity + content-hash equality for EVERY provides.* category (this is the right layer for the parity gate the abandoned deploy tasks proposed for verify-deploy.sh).
  7. Correct the stale prose: the wrong path lua/neotex/shared/extensions/init.lua and the mis-diagnosis in no-task-references-in-deliverables.md; every 'Load Core / Sync all' remediation instruction (deploy-root-guard.sh, check-extension-docs.sh advisory text, regeneration-is-manual-only.md) updated to the new entry points.

SEQUENCING (binding, inherited from the review and from task 966's constraint): task 966 (verify-deploy baseline/delta semantics) must land FIRST — extending verification (item 6) will otherwise create new standing failures that convert multi-task /orchestrate into run-one-then-defer. The dependencies edge encodes this.

VERIFICATION BAR (union of the two subsumed tasks' bars, preserved):
  - A test declaring a new script under scripts/lib/ runs the real headless deploy against a scratch tree and asserts the file lands; same assertion for a re-sync of an already-loaded extension.
  - Declared-vs-deployed parity over the FULL provides.* surface (not just scripts) after a single deploy pass; content-hash equality for a deliberately-staled deployed SKILL.md.
  - Wipe+regenerate round-trip: protected files and settings.local.json survive; new merge-source hook registrations are present after; running it twice is byte-identical.
  - No regression for already-correct entries; the two currently-stale deployed SKILL.md files (skill-orchestrate, skill-orchestrate-hard) are caught by the new verification before the fix and clean after.

SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): deploy machinery edits target lua/neotex/plugins/ai/**; script/rule edits target agent-system/extensions/**; never .claude/**. DELIVERABLE RULE: no task numbers in deliverables outside specs/**; use durable anchors (function names, entry names, script names).

artifacts.summary: Confirms all six root causes from the review with fresh file:line evidence and a fully enumerated 11-function copy_* divergence table; includes concrete recommendations and risks for the implementation plan, including a third bulk-resync path (picker 'Reload All') the plan should also consolidate.

9-phase plan collapsing the two deploy engines onto the manifest-driven loader: scratch-tree regression harness first (red baseline), table-driven copier collapse, force/resync mode plus a single manager.resync_all bulk entry point (absorbing the picker's third Kahn's-algorithm reimplementation), preserved-state snapshot/restore covering .syncprotect paths, corrected regenerate ordering with a wired backup->wipe->restore->clear sequence, entry-point consolidation retiring load_all_globally and the dead is_load_all branch, manifest-driven verification with content-hash parity across all 11 provides.* categories routed through verify-deploy.sh's existing findings accumulator, prose corrections, and end-to-end execution of the union verification bar. Includes 7 dependency waves, 6 scope hypotheses, 2 declared atomic-batch phases, and a rollback path that ships force-resync plus full verification without the wipe if the wipe cannot be made safe.

Full implementation summary for the deploy-engine consolidation: one manifest-driven engine, idempotent load/resync/wipe, full-category content-hash verification, and the prose sweep correcting every stale reference to the retired engine.

Extended post-load verification (verify.lua + verify-deploy.sh's new gate5) to declared-vs-deployed parity plus content-hash equality across all 11 provides.* categories. Fixed a genuine regression found during the final verification-bar execution: a brand-new consuming repo's .syncprotect auto-seed step, present in the retired engine but missing from the new one, is now restored. completed_projects.title: One router: command-route-skill.sh everywhere, manifest-declared agent resolution
completed_projects.description:
Collapse the FIVE independent routing implementations into one. From the agent-system review (specs/reviews/review-2026-07-29-agent-system.md, skills/commands section):

WHAT IS WRONG:
  1. command-route-skill.sh (the canonical router, with the documented 5-step routing_hard ladder) is called by exactly ONE of 48 commands (implement.md ~line 263). research.md and plan.md each carry a ~37-line inline hand-copy of Steps 1-3 that OMITS the hard ladder entirely — so /research N --hard and /plan N --hard resolve the STANDARD skill and the manifest routing_hard entries are never consulted on those paths. This silently defeats hard mode for two of its three commands.
  2. skill-orchestrate (~lines 69-108) and skill-orchestrate-hard (~lines 143-190) carry two MORE routing implementations with OPPOSITE precedence (first-match vs last-match, acknowledged in context/guides/hard-mode-routing.md), and derive agent names by string surgery: sed 's/^skill-//' + '-agent'. Applied to real manifests this produces NON-EXISTENT agents: email -> researcher-agent, memory -> learn-agent, filetypes -> filetypes-agent (real name filetypes-router-agent), present:slides -> slides:assemble-agent. /orchestrate on an email or memory task dispatches to an agent with no file.
  3. skill-orchestrate's extension probe keys manifest path on task_type == directory name, which is false for neovim->nvim, lean4->lean (both masked by hardcoded case arms) and epi->epidemiology (NOT masked — epi silently falls through to general-* agents).
  4. routing_exempt:true is documented as identifying THE core manifest but is set by three manifests (core, literature, slidev); the loop breaks on the first glob hit and resolves to core only because 'core' sorts first alphabetically. An extension named e.g. 'base' would silently shadow core's routing_hard table.
  5. skill-orchestrator/SKILL.md is a vestigial sixth table (knows only general|meta|markdown), byte-identical to its own SKILL.md.archived twin, with one live consumer (epidemiology/commands/epi.md) — yet adding-domains.md and copy-claude-directory.md still instruct developers to update it.

WORK:
  1. Make research.md and plan.md call command-route-skill.sh exactly as implement.md does; delete the inline copies.
  2. Add explicit agent routing to the manifests (e.g. routing_agents or derive from provides.agents) and make both orchestrate engines resolve agents from it; delete the sed-based derivation and both hardcoded case tables; unify precedence to the documented first-match-wins ladder.
  3. Fix the manifest probe to resolve extension directory from task_type via the manifests themselves (scan for the manifest whose routing declares the task_type), not directory-name guessing.
  4. Key core-manifest identification on .name == "core" (or equivalent unique key) instead of routing_exempt; keep routing_exempt for its exemption semantics only.
  5. Retire skill-orchestrator: fold its one consumer (epi.md) onto the canonical router, delete the .archived twin, and fix the two guides that still reference it.

VERIFICATION BAR:
  - /research N --hard on a general task resolves skill-researcher-hard via the manifest routing_hard entry (assert with the router's stderr trace); same for /plan.
  - /orchestrate routing resolution for every task_type declared in any loaded manifest yields an agent file that EXISTS on disk (add this as a wiring validation check so the class cannot recur).
  - epi tasks resolve epidemiology agents; email and memory task types resolve real agents or explicitly route to general-* by declaration, not by accident.
  - Both orchestrate engines produce identical routing decisions for an identical (op, task_type) matrix (table-driven test).

SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): edit agent-system/extensions/**, never .claude/**. DELIVERABLE RULE: no task numbers in deliverables outside specs/**.

All 8 phases completed: shared routing library, two thin resolvers, explicit routing_agents manifest declarations, implement.md effort_flag fix, skill-orchestrator retirement, wiring-lint gate7 and 18-assertion parity test.

completed_projects.title: One handoff schema, one writer, one validator
completed_projects.description:
Unify the .orchestrator-handoff.json contract. FOUR disagreeing schemas currently coexist, and the nominal producer has zero callers. This SUBSUMES task 947 (marked abandoned in favor of this task — read its description first). Task 949's cslib-sibling propagation is SPUN OUT to the cslib terminal-metadata task (which depends on this one and encodes its decisions); this task's file scope deliberately excludes cslib agent files so it cannot collide with the cslib summary-format task. Related but NOT subsumed: task 968 (handoff-present corroboration gate — this task simplifies its terrain but 968's gate logic stays separate) and task 973 (reconcile-task-status safe recovery from malformed handoff status — that failure-mode handling stays; this task reduces its trigger frequency).

THE FOUR SCHEMAS (from the review, specs/reviews/review-2026-07-29-agent-system.md):
  1. docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md (~lines 103-140): requires phase, status, summary, artifacts[]{type,path}; blockers as {description, phase, severity}; nested continuation_context.
  2. context/contracts/wrap-up.md (~lines 35-53), what H9 hard-mode agents actually write: no phase/summary/artifacts; requires phases_completed/phases_total, skeleton, sorry_inventory; blockers as {phase, target, verbatim_goal, what_was_tried, why_it_failed}; flat continuation_path.
  3. validate-handoff.sh (~line 106): requires status, phases_completed, phases_total, blockers — neither phase, summary, nor artifacts; validates blockers against the wrap-up shape. A handoff can PASS validation and still starve skill-orchestrate Stage 5 of artifacts[0].path.
  4. The readers' union: both orchestrate engines read .summary, .artifacts[0].{path,type,summary} (artifacts[0].summary is documented NOWHERE), and the two engines read DIFFERENT blocker shapes (base: .blockers as a string from state.json; hard: .blockers[0].verbatim_goal from the handoff). The documented .description field is read by neither engine — dead.
  5. The nominal writer skill_write_orchestrator_handoff (skill-base.sh ~line 585) has ZERO callers — its own header says so. The only live writer is prose in three hard-mode agent files. Base-mode /orchestrate never produces a handoff at all; orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh reconstructs from .return-meta.json. Three reader-side defenses (staleness gate, stray-handoff sweep, recovery bridge) exist solely to absorb this.

WORK:
  1. Decide the ONE schema (a JSON Schema file, like events-schema.json), covering the union the readers actually need: status, phase, summary, artifacts[]{type,path,summary}, phases_completed/total, plan_markers_verified, ONE blocker shape, one continuation form. Settle the research-phase writer question (do research dispatches write a handoff or not — pick one and align agent contracts, wrap-up.md, and the schema's writer table).
  2. Make validate-handoff.sh enforce exactly that schema.
  3. Pick ONE writer: either wire skill_write_orchestrator_handoff into the skills for all three phases (making base-mode handoffs real and retiring the recovery bridge), or delete it and declare .return-meta.json the single return channel with the handoff generated FROM it by the orchestrator. Do not keep both channels with a bridge.
  4. Align both engines' reads (including the blockers divergence) and the three hard-mode agents' H9 prose to the schema. (The cslib agents are deliberately OUT of scope here — the downstream cslib terminal-metadata task propagates this task's decisions to them.)

VERIFICATION BAR:
  - validate-handoff.sh accepts a handoff written by the chosen writer and REJECTS one missing any reader-required field (test both directions).
  - Both orchestrate engines extract identical fields from an identical handoff fixture; no reader jq path references a field absent from the schema (grep-audit).
  - A full /orchestrate cycle on a scratch task produces a schema-valid handoff (or, if return-meta is chosen, no handoff and no recovery-bridge warnings).

SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): edit agent-system/extensions/**, never .claude/**. DELIVERABLE RULE: no task numbers in deliverables outside specs/**.

completed_projects.title: Extract shared skill stage blocks as imports; route all skills through skill-base.sh
completed_projects.description:
Apply the lit-stage4a-flow.md pattern (ONE shared, directly-executable block imported by @-reference — the single best-factored block in the system, whose own header documents the drift class it fixed) to the rest of the skill lifecycle, and make skills call the skill-base.sh functions that already exist instead of hand-copying them.

  - 41 skills hand-write the .postflight-pending heredoc; the copies have diverged into FOUR incompatible marker shapes (skill-base.sh's skill_create_postflight_marker omits task_number; standard skills add it; hard skills also DROP the behavioral stop_hook_active field; team skills add team_size and drop created/stop_hook_active).
  - 41 hand-written cleanup blocks, 17 hand-written preflight calls, 11 TTS blocks — against skill_preflight_update, skill_create_postflight_marker, skill_cleanup already in skill-base.sh (sourced by only 8 files).

completed_projects.title: Context budget enforcement: demote always-load bloat, break the meta catch-all, one index schema
completed_projects.description:
Bring context loading back within its own declared budgets and give index entries ONE schema authority. DEPENDS ON the index-validator repair task (truthful line counts are the precondition for any budget work).

completed_projects.title: Fix git-commit-scoped.sh .lock exclude pathspec aborting git add and silently dropping commits
completed_projects.description:
SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): `.claude/**` is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and NEVER `.claude/**`. Runtime invocations may still reference deployed `.claude/scripts/*` paths -- that is the CALL PATH, not the EDIT TARGET.

LINE-NUMBER CAVEAT: anchor on symbol names and quoted strings, never on line numbers.

WHAT IS WRONG: `git-commit-scoped.sh` auto-injects a canonical ephemeral-runtime-file exclusion set for any task-directory pathspec entry (the `case "$p" in specs/[0-9][0-9][0-9]_*/)` block). One of the four injected entries is `":(exclude)${task_dir}/.lock/"`. When the `.lock` directory actually EXISTS -- which is exactly when a task lock is held -- naming it in an explicit `:(exclude)` pathspec makes `git add` treat it as an explicitly-named path and refuse the WHOLE add with "The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files", exiting 1. `git-commit-scoped.sh` then takes its `if ! git add "${pathspecs[@]}"` branch, prints "WARNING: git add failed for one or more staged paths (non-blocking); no commit was attempted." and exits 2. The commit does not happen. Because the failure is by-design non-blocking, every caller logs the warning and continues, so a dropped commit is silent in practice.

REPRODUCED EMPIRICALLY (not code review), against a scratch task dir containing a `.lock/` directory and one ordinary file:
  git add --dry-run "specs/NNN_probe/" ":(exclude)specs/NNN_probe/.lock/"   -> rc=1, "paths are ignored"
  git add --dry-run "specs/NNN_probe/"                                       -> rc=0
The `.gitignore` rule that makes `.lock` ignored is the `**/.lock/` entry.

WHY THIS IS SYSTEMIC, NOT INCIDENTAL: `skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md` Stage MT-4 orders the per-task scoped commit at step 5.5 BEFORE the per-task lock release at step 6. That ordering is deliberate and documented (a failed commit must never withhold the lock release). It also means the `.lock` directory is present by construction at every multi-task per-task commit, so this defect is on the normal path for `/orchestrate` multi-task postflight, not an edge case. Observed live three times in a single two-task `/orchestrate` batch.

CORRECT A WRONG WORKAROUND ALREADY IN CIRCULATION: two implementation agents independently recorded the workaround as "omit the trailing slash on the task-directory pathspec" and captured it as a memory candidate. That is FALSE and was verified false -- `git add "specs/NNN_probe" ":(exclude)specs/NNN_probe/.lock/"` (no trailing slash) fails identically with rc=1. The trigger is the `:(exclude)` entry naming a gitignored path, not the trailing slash on the positive entry. Any memory carrying the trailing-slash claim must be corrected or purged as part of this task, or it will keep sending future agents down a workaround that does not work.

WORK:
  1. Fix the injection so a held lock cannot abort the add. Evaluate the options rather than assuming one: drop the `.lock/` entry entirely (the other three ephemeral excludes name paths that are NOT gitignored, so they do not have this problem, and `.lock/` is already covered by `**/.lock/` in `.gitignore` -- git never stages an ignored path from a directory pathspec anyway, which is precisely why the exclude is redundant); or keep it but make the add tolerant. Prefer the minimal change that provably restores rc=0 while still never staging `.lock`.
  2. Keep the exclusion set in `agent-system/extensions/core/context/standards/git-staging-scope.md` in sync -- it publishes the same four-entry `ephemeral_excludes` array in two places, and `git-commit-scoped.sh`'s comment states it "Mirrors context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's ephemeral_excludes array exactly". Script and standard must not drift.
  3. Do NOT weaken the V2/V3 safety gates or the `specs/.commit-lock/` mutex behavior while doing this.

VERIFICATION BAR:
  - A regression test that creates a task dir containing a `.lock/` directory plus a tracked file, runs the real `git-commit-scoped.sh`, and asserts the commit ACTUALLY LANDS (verify via `git log`, not merely a zero exit).
  - Assert `.lock` is still not staged in that same test -- fixing the abort must not start committing lock directories.
  - `bash -n` clean on the edited script.
  - Existing callers unaffected: a commit with no `.lock` present still succeeds and still excludes the other three ephemeral runtime files.

DELIVERABLE RULE: this task's own deliverables outside `specs/**` must not cite task numbers; use durable anchors (script names, function names, pathspec strings).

completed_projects.title: Extend plan-heading evidence corroboration to the handoff-present completion path
completed_projects.description:
SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): `.claude/**` is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and NEVER `.claude/**`.

LINE-NUMBER CAVEAT: anchor on symbol names and quoted strings, never on line numbers.

WHAT IS WRONG: `skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md` has an "Evidence corroboration" block that repairs missing phase accounting by counting `[COMPLETED]` / `[COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS]` phase headings in the plan file via the shared `scripts/lib/phase-heading-patterns.sh` anchors. That block is reachable ONLY on the return-meta recovery path -- its precondition is `evidence_suspect=true` AND `evidence_reason="PHASES_ZERO_ON_SUCCESS"` AND `dispatch_status="implemented"`, and `evidence_suspect` is a field emitted by `orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh`, which only runs when the handoff is MISSING or STALE.

There is no equivalent corroboration for the handoff-PRESENT path. `phases_completed` / `phases_total` are documented as OPTIONAL top-level handoff fields (see `docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md`). When a dispatch writes a handoff by hand (jq) reporting `status: "implemented"` but omits those optional fields, Stage 5 reads them as `// 0`, `plan_markers_verified` resolves to `"absent"`, and `skill_gate_completion_claim` takes its conservative case-3 branch and REFUSES the completion transition. The task is left at `implementing` with no `completion_summary`, despite the plan being fully closed.

OBSERVED LIVE (empirical, not code review): a 10-phase meta task finished with all 10 phase headings marked `[COMPLETED]` in its plan and its full verification bar passing, but its handoff carried `phases_completed: null, phases_total: null, plan_markers_verified: null`. The completion gate refused, the task stranded at `implementing`, and completion required a human-driven corroboration -- counting plan headings by hand, confirming 10/10, and calling `skill_gate_completion_claim` with the corrected counts. Note the asymmetry this exposes: the identical evidence (plan headings) is trusted automatically when NO handoff exists, and ignored when a handoff exists but is merely incomplete. The weaker-evidence case is handled and the stronger-evidence case is not.

MECHANISM ALREADY BUILT -- REUSE, DO NOT RE-INVENT: `scripts/lib/phase-heading-patterns.sh` publishes `PHASE_HEADING_ERE`, `PHASE_HEADING_DONE_ERE`, `has_nonconforming_phase_headings`, and `warn_nonconforming`. The existing corroboration block already sources it and already handles the three outcomes correctly (non-conforming headings -> unreliable, leave absent; all closed -> correct the counts and set `plan_markers_verified="true"`; partial -> leave untouched, explicitly NOT a second trigger). The fix is to make that same logic reachable from the handoff-present branch, not to write new counting logic.

WORK (decide between these, do not assume -- they are not mutually exclusive):
  A. Extend the corroboration trigger to the handoff-present path: when a fresh handoff reports `status: "implemented"` but `phases_total` resolves to 0 / null, run the SAME plan-heading corroboration before calling `skill_gate_completion_claim`. Preserve the existing false-positive guard: a plan with zero phase headings, or a genuinely partial plan, must still leave `plan_markers_verified="absent"` and the counts untouched.
  B. Close the producer side: make the implementation-agent contracts populate `phases_completed`/`phases_total` whenever they hand-write a handoff. `skill_write_orchestrator_handoff` in `skill-base.sh` already defaults `ORCHESTRATOR_HANDOFF_PHASES_COMPLETED:-0`, so agents using the helper are fine; the gap is agents composing the handoff with a raw `jq -n`.
  C. If A is adopted, mirror it into the multi-task path (`skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md` Stage MT-4 step 2/3) and into `skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md`'s single-task Stage 5, so the three engines do not drift. The MT stage already carries an "identical mirror" of the recovery-path corroboration block -- match that precedent.

CONSTRAINT -- DO NOT WEAKEN THE GATE: `skill_gate_completion_claim`'s fail-closed posture is deliberate and must survive. Case 1 (phase accounting present and INCOMPLETE) must still always refuse. This task makes MORE INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE available to the gate; it must never make the gate accept an uncorroborated claim. A corroborated correction must come from the plan file (an independent artifact), never from the incomplete handoff's own values.

VERIFICATION BAR:
  - A fixture where a handoff reports `implemented` with null phase counts AND the plan shows all phases closed -> completion is ALLOWED, with the `[UNVERIFIED PHASES CORROBORATED]` banner emitted.
  - A fixture where a handoff reports `implemented` with null phase counts AND the plan shows a PARTIAL close -> completion is still REFUSED.
  - A fixture where the plan has zero conforming phase headings -> completion is still REFUSED, with the non-conforming warning emitted.
  - `bash -n` clean on every edited file's embedded bash.
  - The three engines (base single-task, base multi-task, hard single-task) agree, or any remaining divergence is documented in-file as deliberate the way the existing `blocked`-row divergence already is.

DELIVERABLE RULE: this task's own deliverables outside `specs/**` must not cite task numbers; use durable anchors.

Those writes remain hand-rolled `jq > tmp && mv` sequences with no `.scope-lock` acquisition, no `jq empty` validation before the `mv`, and no serialization against a concurrent writer -- exactly the class of unprotected write the mutex convention exists to eliminate.

This was identified and deliberately scoped OUT of the conversion work that routed all `specs/state.json` writers through `state-write.sh` (the verification bar there was worded as `specs/state.json`-targeted only, so archive/vault sites were left hand-rolled ON PURPOSE, with mechanism-naming comments, rather than force-converted against a mechanism that cannot address them). completed_projects.title: Loosen implementation agents' plan-checklist match off the literal **Task {P}.{N}**: prefix
completed_projects.description:
Loosen the plan-checklist mark-completed instruction in the implementation agents so it matches checklist items by their existing text rather than by a literal `**Task {P}.{N}**:` prefix.

SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): the agent-system SOURCE of truth is agent-system/extensions/. The .claude/ tree is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target agent-system/extensions/** and NEVER .claude/**. The source store lives at /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/, NOT in the cslib repo. The user reloads the agent system via a <leader>al keybinding which redeploys from this nvim source store to cslib and other repos, so the fix must land there to propagate.

OBSERVED FAILURE (live, verified during an /orchestrate run in the cslib repo, not hypothetical): plan checklist items were never ticked. A plan carried 87 checklist items and 0 were marked complete even though 4 phases were genuinely finished.

ROOT CAUSE - SHAPE MISMATCH (verified by direct file inspection of the source store): general-implementation-agent.md instructs a literal Edit match on `- [ ] **Task {P}.{N}**: {description}` (12 occurrences of that prefix form, concentrated at lines ~187-201 and ~300-302). But planner-agent.md emits FREE-FORM PROSE checklist items - see agent-system/extensions/core/agents/planner-agent.md lines ~237-238 (`- [ ] {Step 1}` / `- [ ] {Step 2}`) and ~267-268 (`- [ ] {Test criterion 1}`). Zero of the 87 items in the observed plan matched the literal prefix shape. So even a correctly-instructed agent matches nothing, and it fails SILENTLY - the Edit simply finds no match and the agent proceeds.

SCOPE - three files carry the same brittle literal-prefix instruction:
- agent-system/extensions/core/agents/general-implementation-agent.md (12 occurrences)
- agent-system/extensions/lean/agents/lean-implementation-agent.md (3 occurrences)
- agent-system/extensions/nix/agents/nix-implementation-agent.md (5 occurrences)

CHOSEN RESOLUTION (decided, do not relitigate): loosen the INSTRUCTION to match items by their existing text, rather than standardizing planner-agent.md onto the `**Task {P}.{N}**:` prefix. Rationale: (a) the brittle literal-prefix match is precisely what made this fail silently; (b) the free-form prose items are more readable in plans; (c) empirically confirmed workable - instructing an agent to match by prose text took the observed plan from 0/87 to 7/87 ticked in a single session. planner-agent.md is therefore NOT edited by this task.

THIS TASK ESTABLISHES CANONICAL WORDING. Two downstream tasks copy the loosened phrasing verbatim into agents that currently have no mark-completed instruction at all. Write the instruction so it is directly reusable: it must tell the agent to locate the checklist item by its existing item text and rewrite the leading `- [ ]` to `- [x]`, appending the `*(completed)*` marker, without depending on any particular item-title format. Preserve the existing deviation-annotation formats (skipped / altered / deferred), which are a separate concern and are already correct.

KNOCK-ON EFFECT TO BE AWARE OF (context, not extra scope): agent-system/extensions/core/skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md line ~1044 defines the drift-inspection prompt, which computes `completed_items` by counting `- [x]`. Because nothing was ever ticked, that metric reported 0 completed and drift_pct 0.0 - reading as "no work done" while 4 phases were complete. The drift metric stays dead until this task and its downstream siblings land. No edit to skill-orchestrate is required here; the metric becomes correct once items are actually ticked.

VERIFICATION: after the edit, confirm no remaining instruction in the three files requires the literal `**Task {P}.{N}**:` prefix in order to mark an item complete, and that the deviation-annotation formats are unchanged.

completed_projects.title: Make reconcile-task-status.sh recover from a malformed handoff status instead of refusing promotion
completed_projects.description:
Give reconcile-task-status.sh a defined, safe recovery behavior when .orchestrator-handoff.json carries a status outside the normative vocabulary, instead of silently refusing promotion and wedging the task.

SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): the agent-system SOURCE of truth is agent-system/extensions/. The .claude/ tree is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target agent-system/extensions/** and NEVER .claude/**. The source store lives at /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/, NOT in the cslib repo. The user reloads the agent system via a <leader>al keybinding which redeploys from this nvim source store to cslib and other repos, so the fix must land there to propagate.

FILE: agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/reconcile-task-status.sh

THE DEFECT - AN ASYMMETRY (verified by direct inspection, lines 186-195, recorded here verbatim because it is the actual defect and is easy to lose in paraphrase):

    handoff_permits_promotion() {
      local expected_status="$1"
      local handoff_file="${TASK_DIR}/.orchestrator-handoff.json"
      if [[ ! -f "$handoff_file" ]]; then
        return 0
      fi
      local handoff_status
      handoff_status=$(jq -r '.status // ""' "$handoff_file" 2>/dev/null)
      [[ "$handoff_status" == "$expected_status" ]]
    }

A MISSING handoff returns 0 at the `[[ ! -f "$handoff_file" ]]` early return - promotion is PERMITTED. A MALFORMED one falls through to the exact string equality test `[[ "$handoff_status" == "$expected_status" ]]` and REFUSES. A malformed handoff is therefore treated STRICTLY WORSE than no handoff at all, which is backwards: the no-handoff case is the one carrying less information.

OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE (live, verified, not hypothetical): during an /orchestrate run in the cslib repo, cslib-research-agent wrote `"status": "success"` into .orchestrator-handoff.json (and `"research_complete"` into .return-meta.json); neither value is in the closed six-value vocabulary researched|planned|implemented|partial|failed|blocked defined in docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md and context/formats/return-metadata-file.md. TWO independent guards then both rejected it:
1. skill-orchestrate Stage 5 Tier C halted the run on cycle 1.
2. This guard ALSO refused promotion.

Because of guard 2, the documented recovery path - "re-run /orchestrate, entry reconcile repairs it" - DID NOT WORK. The task was genuinely wedged and required MANUAL normalization of the status fields in both .orchestrator-handoff.json and .return-meta.json to unstick it.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE EXISTING AGENT-CONTRACT TASK CHAIN (important, prevents duplicate/conflicting work): three not_started tasks already own the AGENT-CONTRACT half of this incident - settling whether research agents may write handoffs at all, adding a Stage 7 final-metadata contract to cslib-research-agent.md, and propagating the artifacts array-of-objects spec to the sibling cslib agents. ALL THREE describe only the orchestrator Stage 5 halt. NONE of them covers this second guard in reconcile-task-status.sh. This task is deliberately standalone and scoped to the SCRIPT behavior; it is a shell-script fix with different verification from that chain's documentation reconciliation. Do NOT fold it back into them, and do NOT re-do their agent-contract work here.

DESIGN TENSION THE FIX MUST RESOLVE RATHER THAN PAPER OVER: the guard's strictness is presumably DELIBERATE - do not promote on an outcome you cannot parse. So the fix is NOT simply to relax the comparison. It needs a DEFINED behavior for the malformed case that is at least as safe as the missing-handoff case the function already permits. Consider, and decide explicitly between, options such as: treating an off-vocabulary status as equivalent to a missing handoff (falling through to whatever evidence the missing-handoff path already relies on, e.g. the .return-meta.json recovery helper); versus refusing promotion but emitting a loud, actionable diagnostic naming the offending value and the legal vocabulary so the operator is not left guessing; versus a narrow normalization of known-bad synonyms. Whichever is chosen, the outcome must not be "silently stuck", and the rationale must be recorded in the script so a future reader does not re-tighten it by reflex.

ALSO CHECK: the sibling helper handoff_status_value() at lines ~197-203 and any other call site that reads the handoff status, so the chosen semantics are applied consistently rather than at one call site only.

VERIFICATION: construct a task directory with an off-vocabulary handoff status and confirm the chosen behavior occurs, that it is at least as permissive as the same directory with the handoff file removed, and that the diagnostic (if that route is chosen) names both the offending value and the legal set.

completed_projects.title: Fix generated CLAUDE.md double-body and duplicate Stop-hook registration
completed_projects.description:
Fix the generated .claude/CLAUDE.md containing its entire body TWICE (~891 duplicated lines, ~13k wasted tokens in every session prompt), plus the doubled claude-stop-notify.sh Stop-hook registration in .claude/settings.json.

WHAT IS WRONG (verified live, from the agent-system review specs/reviews/review-2026-07-29-agent-system.md): two mechanisms both run on every Load/Reload and disagree about who owns the file. (1) generate_claudemd() in lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/merge.lua (~line 549) rewrites the whole file as header..fragments and emits NO section markers. (2) reinject_loaded_extensions() in lua/neotex/plugins/ai/claude/commands/picker/operations/sync.lua (~line 220) then calls merge_mod.inject_section() for every loaded extension 'as defense-in-depth'. inject_section decides idempotency by searching for '<!-- SECTION: core -->' (merge.lua ~line 124) — which step 1 never writes — so it falls through and APPENDS a second full copy. init.lua (~line 83) carries a comment claiming section injection is skipped here, so the two halves of the codebase disagree about ownership. The current deployed .claude/CLAUDE.md is 1801 lines with lines 7-897 and 899-1801 byte-identical modulo markers. Separately, .claude/settings.json registers claude-stop-notify.sh TWICE on Stop — the deep_merge append-without-replace hazard the core manifest's own _comment warns about, now actually occurred.

WORK:
  1. Pick ONE ownership regime and make both code paths agree: either generate_claudemd() emits '<!-- SECTION: id -->' markers for every fragment it writes (so inject_section becomes idempotent), or reinject_loaded_extensions() stops calling inject_section for the claudemd merge key. Note strip_extension_sections()/preserve_sections()/restore_sections() in sync.lua are all built around the marker regime — prefer restoring markers unless research shows otherwise.
  2. De-duplicate the current deployed CLAUDE.md by regenerating after the fix.
  3. Fix the duplicate Stop-hook registration and make the settings merge dedup catch it (deep_equal dedup exists but did not prevent this — determine why).

  - Running the load cycle twice in a row produces a byte-identical CLAUDE.md (idempotency).
  - .claude/settings.json Stop hooks list claude-stop-notify.sh exactly once after redeploy.

completed_projects.title: Wire non-conformance detection into the hard-mode resume-scan sites
completed_projects.description:
SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): `.claude/**` is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and NEVER `.claude/**`.

THIS IS NOT A GRAMMAR-WIDENING TASK. READ THIS PARAGRAPH BEFORE STARTING. The defect was originally reported as "the phase-heading regex cannot match letter-suffixed phases such as `Phase 4A`, so widen it." That framing is WRONG and following it would violate a standing, deliberately re-affirmed decision. `context/formats/plan-format.md`'s "Canonical phase-heading shape" subsection states that letter-suffixed sub-phases are deliberately not supported, that this is a decision rather than an unimplemented feature, and -- explicitly -- that the correct general fix for the observed gap is LOUD NON-CONFORMANCE DETECTION rather than a widened grammar, because "widening admits exactly one new token shape and leaves the next unanticipated one (`3-alt`, `III`) just as silent as before." An author reaching for `4A` should write `4.1`. DO NOT widen `PHASE_HEADING_ERE`.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT (verified in the source store, still present): both hard-mode resume-scan sites select the next phase with a grep of the form `grep -E "${PHASE_HEADING_ERE} .*${PHASE_STATUS_OPEN_ERE}" "$plan_path" | head -1`. Because `PHASE_HEADING_ERE` filters to CONFORMING headings only, a non-conforming heading is not merely unmatched -- it is INVISIBLE to the scan. The library's `warn_nonconforming` / `has_nonconforming_phase_headings` detection can therefore NEVER fire on this path, because the grep has already discarded the offending line before any conformance check runs. The two sites do call `warn_nonconforming`, but only in the branch where `next_heading` is non-empty and `extract_phase_number` fails -- a state that is unreachable, since the grep only ever yields lines that already match `PHASE_HEADING_ERE`.

OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE: a plan using `4A`/`4B`/`4C` had `### Phase 4C: ... [IN PROGRESS]` skipped entirely and `### Phase 5: ... [NOT STARTED]` selected instead. `extract_phase_number` then succeeded cleanly on `5`, so nothing warned. The orchestrator would have dispatched work OUT OF ORDER, on top of an unfinished phase. Caught and worked around by hand during a live run.

So the loud-non-conformance contract that `plan-format.md` declares CLOSED ("This is a closed contract, not an aspiration") is in fact not wired at these two sites. That is the gap to close.

WORK: at each resume-scan site, run a conformance check over the WHOLE plan file BEFORE trusting the filtered scan result -- e.g. call `has_nonconforming_phase_headings "$plan_path"` (NOT the racy `nonconforming_phase_headings | grep -q .` pipe form; the library header explains why) and, when it reports findings, emit `warn_nonconforming` and take the loud INCONCLUSIVE branch rather than silently proceeding with a possibly-out-of-order selection. Match each site's existing posture: `skill-implementer-hard` currently hard-stops (`exit 1`) on a non-conforming heading, while `skill-orchestrate-hard` warns and leaves `next_phase` empty -- decide deliberately whether those two postures should remain different, and record the reasoning. Then audit whether any OTHER site in the source store performs a conforming-only filter and inherits the same blind spot; the library's own header documents that consumers are found live via `grep -rl 'phase-heading-patterns.sh' agent-system/extensions`.

EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY RATIONALE: depends on the in-flight phase-heading unification task (owns both edited files and the library itself) and on the residual state.json writer conversion task (lists `skills/skill-implementer-hard/SKILL.md` in its file_scope). Also chained behind the sibling Stage 4 repair task, which edits the same `skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md`.

VERIFICATION BAR: a plan containing `### Phase 4C: ... [IN PROGRESS]` followed by `### Phase 5: ... [NOT STARTED]` produces a LOUD named warning identifying the `4C` heading by line number, and does NOT silently select phase 5. A fully conforming plan resolves its next phase exactly as before (no behavior change on the happy path). `bash -n` clean.

completed_projects.title: Add staleness detection to the orchestrator loop-guard resume path
completed_projects.description:
SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): `.claude/**` is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and NEVER `.claude/**`.

DEFECT: the Stage 2 resume branch of `skills/skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md` trusts ANY syntactically valid `.orchestrator-loop-guard` unconditionally. The guard is accepted on the sole condition `[ -f "$loop_guard_file" ] && jq empty "$loop_guard_file"` -- no freshness signal of any kind is consulted before its `cycle_count`, `burnout_signals_this_session`, and `infra_failures` counters are adopted as the current run's state.

OBSERVED (live run): a guard 13 DAYS STALE was encountered, originating from a SUPERSEDED plan lineage (it referenced an early plan version while the live plan was many versions later) and carrying a `max_cycles` value from an older skill version, while the actual current work ran under a different lineage entirely. Trusting it would have resumed at cycle 11 of 13, leaving 2 usable cycles on a counter that never counted ANY of the live lineage's work. `context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md` and the Stage 2 prose already DOCUMENT this hazard as unguarded; the gap is that nothing DETECTS it.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT -- READ BEFORE CHOOSING A SIGNAL. The obvious fix (compare `session_id`) is explicitly ruled out by a sibling decision a few lines below in the same Stage 2 block. The churn-state file's `session_id` handling is annotated: "Observational-only session_id tracking (NEVER a gate ... SESSION_ID is regenerated per /orchestrate invocation, while this file is explicitly designed to survive across conversational turns. The real same-task concurrency guard is task-lock.sh's acquire/heartbeat/release mutex, not session_id equality)." A `session_id` equality gate on the loop guard would directly contradict that rationale and would break legitimate conversational resume, which is the guard's whole purpose. So this task must find a DIFFERENT staleness signal. Candidates to evaluate, not a prescription: mtime age against a threshold; plan lineage (does the guard's referenced plan version still match the live plan?); schema/version drift (the guard's persisted `max_cycles` disagreeing with the skill's current `MAX_CYCLES` constant is direct evidence the guard predates the running skill version). A combination may be warranted; whatever is chosen, the reasoning belongs in `orchestrator-runtime-files.md` alongside the existing two-class policy.

WORK: (1) Decide what counts as stale, and record the decision and its rationale in `context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md`, explicitly addressing why the chosen signal does not fall to the same objection that disqualifies `session_id`. (2) Implement detection on the Stage 2 resume path. (3) On detection, ARCHIVE ASIDE AND REINITIALIZE rather than either silently trusting or silently resetting -- preserve the stale guard as evidence, following the same "preserve the evidence" shape the existing stray-handoff sweep already uses, and emit a loud named notice. Silent reset is only marginally better than silent trust; both destroy the operator's ability to understand what happened. (4) Consider whether `.orchestrator-churn-state.json` warrants the same treatment -- it has the identical unguarded-read shape and the same documented hazard -- and either extend the fix to it or record why it does not need it.

EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY RATIONALE: chained behind the sibling tasks editing the same `skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md`.

VERIFICATION BAR: a loop guard whose staleness signal trips is archived to a preserved path (not deleted), a fresh guard is initialized at cycle 0, and a loud named notice identifies which signal tripped and where the old guard was preserved. A genuinely current guard resumes exactly as before, and an ordinary cross-conversational-turn resume is NOT falsely flagged (this is the regression that a naive `session_id` gate would cause -- test it explicitly). `bash -n` clean.

completed_projects.title: Correct the pr_ready skill text and docs to describe the actual resulting state
completed_projects.description:
SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): `.claude/**` is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and NEVER `.claude/**`.

THIS IS A DOCUMENTATION AND SKILL-TEXT ACCURACY FIX, NOT A SCRIPT CHANGE. READ THIS PARAGRAPH BEFORE STARTING. The defect was originally reported as "the skeleton-exhaustion branch asserts `--allow-pr-ready` is a sanctioned exception, but `update-task-status.sh` refuses `pr_ready` for non-`pr` task types and routes to `completed` instead -- decide which side is authoritative." Investigation found the two artifacts ALREADY AGREE and no script change is warranted:
  - `scripts/update-task-status.sh` DOES honor `--allow-pr-ready`: its guard reads `elif [[ "$target_status" == "pr_ready" && "$ALLOW_PR_READY" == "true" ]]` with the comment "allowed: explicit override flag passed (e.g. skeleton-exhaustion routing in skill-orchestrate-hard)". The script's own comment names this exact call site as sanctioned.
  - The reason the live run nonetheless landed on `completed` is a SEPARATE, correct mapping in the same script: on `postflight` with target `pr_ready`, `STATE_STATUS` is set to `completed`. So the flag is accepted AND the task still comes to rest at `completed`.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: because of that mapping, a non-`pr` task never RESTS at `pr_ready`. The documented policy statement (`[PR READY]` is type=pr only; `[IMPLEMENTING] -> [COMPLETED]` is the terminus for all non-`pr` types) is therefore TRUE of resting states, and the apparent conflict is narrower than a three-way policy contradiction. The inaccurate artifact is `skills/skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md`'s own prose in the skeleton-exhaustion branch, which says "Transition to `pr_ready`" and exits with `EXIT (success, pr_ready -- skeleton exhausted, ...)`. Both MISDESCRIBE the state that actually results. An operator reading the exit line reasonably concludes the task is parked at `[PR READY]` awaiting PR submission, when it has in fact come to rest at `[COMPLETED]`.

WORK: (1) Correct the skeleton-exhaustion branch's prose and EXIT line to describe the state that actually results, naming the `postflight:pr_ready -> completed` mapping so a future reader is not surprised by it. (2) Re-examine the inline comment claiming `--allow-pr-ready` is "the sanctioned task-type-agnostic exception" -- the flag IS honored, so the claim is not false, but it is misleading in isolation because it omits that the resulting resting state is `completed` regardless. Make it accurate. (3) Check whether the CLAUDE.md merge source needs a clarifying sentence distinguishing TRANSITION targets from RESTING states, since the current wording invites exactly the misreading that produced this defect report. (4) DO NOT change `update-task-status.sh`'s guard or its status mapping; both are correct as written. If implementation reveals a genuine reason to change the script, STOP and escalate rather than proceeding -- that would be a policy change, not the accuracy fix this task is scoped to.

OBSERVED: every cslib task trips non-blocking gate-out format errors on its implementation summary (measured on one real task: 4 errors, 4 fields auto-repaired). cslib summaries come out headed `## What Was Done` / `## Verification` / `## Plan Deviations` / `## Task Completion Assessment`, while `agent-system/extensions/core/context/formats/summary-format.md` requires `## Overview` / `## What Changed` / `## Decisions` / `## Impacts` / `## Follow-ups` / `## References`.

CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (the reported cause was wrong; verify before acting). The divergence is NOT a competing cslib template overriding the standard -- no cslib file declares `## What Was Done` or `## Task Completion Assessment` anywhere. Two real findings replace that framing:
  (a) `extensions/cslib/agents/cslib-implementation-agent.md` contains ZERO references to `summary-format.md`. It is never loaded, so the agent has no template to follow and improvises headings into the vacuum. Its only summary-structure instruction is a lone MUST-DO: "Include `## Plan Deviations` section in implementation summary." By contrast the four core/extension implementation agents that DO conform (general, nvim, nix, web) all reference the standard.
  (b) `extensions/cslib/agents/cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md` DOES load `summary-format.md` -- and ALSO mandates `## Plan Deviations`, a section the standard does not contain. That agent is therefore instructed to satisfy two requirements that cannot both be met, which is a live internal contradiction independent of finding (a).

DECISION REQUIRED (pick one deliberately and record why; do not leave `## Plan Deviations` in its current unresolved status): either (i) cslib conforms fully -- fold plan-deviation content into the standard's existing `## Decisions` or `## Follow-ups` sections and drop the bespoke heading, or (ii) the standard formally ADMITS `## Plan Deviations` as a recognized optional section, in which case `summary-format.md` must say so and the gate-out validator must accept it. Option (ii) is a change to a shared core standard and affects every extension, so it needs explicit justification, not a default.

WORK: (1) Make the decision above. (2) Add a `summary-format.md` reference to `cslib-implementation-agent.md`'s context-loading section so it stops improvising. (3) Resolve the hard agent's contradiction consistently with the decision. (4) Audit whether any OTHER extension implementation agent omits the `summary-format.md` reference and inherits the same improvisation failure mode -- the four named above conform, but the audit should cover all extensions rather than assuming.

VERIFICATION BAR: a cslib implementation summary produces ZERO gate-out format errors and ZERO auto-repaired fields. Both cslib implementation agents reference `summary-format.md`. No agent is left instructed to emit a section the standard forbids, nor to omit one it requires.

completed_projects.title: Repair /refresh orphan detection so live system and session processes are never selected
completed_projects.description:
SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): `.claude/**` is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and NEVER `.claude/**`.

SEVERITY AND SEQUENCING: this is the highest-severity defect found in its discovery session and SHOULD BE TAKEN FIRST, ahead of the other agent-system tasks created alongside it. It carries no dependency edges (no file_scope collision with any in-flight work), so that ordering is advisory priority, not an enforced constraint -- nothing blocks it and it blocks nothing. It is the only defect in its batch whose failure mode is destructive rather than procedural.

WHAT IS WRONG: `/refresh`'s orphaned-process matcher misidentifies live system and session processes as orphans. Running `/refresh --force` against a live machine would terminate a system daemon and live sessions' processes, including the session issuing the command. Run in read-only status mode against a live machine, the script reported "11 orphaned processes using 57.4 MB". Every one was a false positive.

ROOT CAUSE 1 -- OVER-BROAD MATCH. `get_claude_processes()` (`scripts/claude-refresh.sh:107`) greps `[c]laude|[n]ode.*claude|[a]nthropic` against whole `ps aux` lines, i.e. the full argv, and `get_orphaned_processes()` (`:112`) then filters `$7 == "?"` (the TTY column). `TTY == "?"` is true of EVERY systemd-managed process by definition, so it is not a discriminator at all; combined with a substring match anywhere in argv, any process merely MENTIONING `claude` in an argument is captured. Candidate hardening: require ownership by the invoking UID (excludes the `earlyoom` service user), exclude anything whose cgroup is under `/system.slice/` (system services are never Claude Code orphans), and match on the EXECUTABLE rather than anywhere in argv.

ROOT CAUSE 2 -- THE STATED SAFETY PROPERTY DOES NOT HOLD. The header claims at `scripts/claude-refresh.sh:13` that the script "Excludes current process and parent process tree". It does not. `is_in_current_tree()` (`:54-66`) walks `ppid` UPWARD only. The invoker's own sleep inhibitor is a SIBLING of the invoker's parent -- both are children of `systemd --user` -- not an ancestor, so an ancestor-walk can never reach it. This is a structural impossibility, not a tuning problem. Genuine orphan detection needs a LIVENESS TEST on the process each inhibitor is actually holding open: each carries `tail --pid=<claude_pid>` in its own argv, so the correct predicate is "is `<claude_pid>` still alive?", not "is this process in my ancestry?". Under that predicate every inhibitor observed was correctly live and none was an orphan.

These two root causes MUST be co-fixed. Either landing alone leaves the tool unsafe.

OBSERVED FALSE POSITIVES (all 11 were false; representative set):
- PID 1002 -- `earlyoom.service`, a NixOS SYSTEM daemon, UID `earlyoom`, PPID 1, cgroup `/system.slice/earlyoom.service`. Matched ONLY because its own argv contains the literal string `claude` inside a regex: `--prefer ^(lean|lake|claude|node|npm|opencode)$`. Terminating it DISABLES THE MACHINE'S OUT-OF-MEMORY PROTECTION.
- PID 1905663 -- the invoking session's OWN sleep inhibitor: `systemd-inhibit ... tail --pid=1905591`, where 1905591 is the `claude` process in the invoker's own ancestry, same WezTerm cgroup. Kills the inhibitor of the very session running `/refresh`.
- PID 2205459 -- `claude-memory-tracker`, a live user service. Stops memory tracking.
- PIDs 527856 and 2846183 -- sleep inhibitors of a DIFFERENT live session, whose `claude` PID 527780 was still running and 2 days old. That machine would sleep mid-session.
- PIDs 3658641 and 3658642 -- the refresh script's OWN subshells. Self-termination.

ESCALATION -- UNATTENDED HOURLY AMPLIFICATION. `systemd/claude-refresh.service` ships `ExecStart=%h/.config/nvim/.claude/scripts/claude-refresh.sh --force`, paired with `systemd/claude-refresh.timer` (`OnCalendar=hourly`, `Persistent=true`), and `scripts/install-systemd-timer.sh:104` writes the same `--force` line. So the defective matcher is wired to an hourly, unattended, no-confirmation killer for anyone who runs the shipped installer. Verified NOT installed on the discovery machine (`systemctl --user is-enabled claude-refresh.timer` returns `not-found`) -- latent, not live -- but it ships in that state.

DECIDED POLICY (settled by the user; NOT an implementer judgment call): the timer default becomes NON-DESTRUCTIVE. The timer REPORTS or LOGS rather than terminating, and `--force` becomes a deliberate opt-in. Rationale to record in the change: a matcher bug must never again be amplifiable into unattended hourly kills, regardless of how correct the matcher looks at review time. Apply this to both `systemd/claude-refresh.service` and the `ExecStart` line that `scripts/install-systemd-timer.sh` generates, so a fresh install and an existing unit converge on the same posture.

DEFECT 3 -- NO PREVIEW PATH FOR PROCESS CLEANUP (narrower than first reported; do not overstate it). `scripts/claude-refresh.sh`'s argument loop (`:28-47`) accepts only `--force` and `--help|-h` and exits 1 on anything else, INCLUDING `--dry-run`. However `/refresh --dry-run` does NOT currently crash: `skills/skill-refresh/SKILL.md:40` passes only `--force` or nothing, so the rejection is never actually triggered. The real defect is that the process-cleanup half has NO PREVIEW PATH AT ALL, while `commands/refresh.md` documents `--dry-run` as "Preview both process and directory cleanup". The doc claim is false; the flag is not crashing. Add a genuine preview path and reconcile the doc.

DEFECT 4 -- WRONG RECLAIM FIGURE. `orphan_mem` (`scripts/claude-refresh.sh:155`) is computed from the UNFILTERED orphan list, before the current-tree exclusion at `:172-188` runs. The reported "memory that can be reclaimed" is therefore wrong independently of the matcher bugs. Compute it from the post-exclusion list.

DOC SITES ASSERTING THE FALSE SAFETY PROPERTY (all three must be reconciled with the fixed behavior, not left claiming a property the code lacks): the header comment block at `scripts/claude-refresh.sh:11-14`; the "Process Safety" section of `skills/skill-refresh/SKILL.md` ("Excludes current process tree"); and the "Process Protection" section of `commands/refresh.md` (same claim, plus the `--dry-run` description above).

INVESTIGATED AND DISMISSED -- DO NOT RE-OPEN. It was initially suspected that `commands/refresh.md`'s documented Directory Cleanup section (`projects/`, `debug/`, `file-history/`, `todos/`, `session-env/`, `telemetry/`, `shell-snapshots/`, `plugins/cache/`, `cache/`) described unimplemented behavior, or that a second script was missing from the deploy. THIS IS NOT A DEFECT. `scripts/claude-cleanup.sh` EXISTS at 13,811 bytes in BOTH the source store and the deploy, and `skills/skill-refresh/SKILL.md` Steps 6-7 invoke it. `claude-refresh.sh` is process-only BY DESIGN; directory cleanup is a separate, working script. This is also unrelated to the deploy-propagation task tracked separately. No work is required here; this paragraph exists solely so a future implementer does not re-derive and re-open it.

RELATED BUT NON-BLOCKING: the new regression-test file is a NEW file under `scripts/tests/`, which is exactly the "new files may not reach an existing deploy" class covered by the separate deploy-propagation task. This does NOT gate this task -- the four existing tests in `scripts/tests/` run from the source store -- but do not be surprised if the new test is absent from `.claude/scripts/tests/` until that separate fix lands.

VERIFICATION BAR / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. REGRESSION TESTS ARE A HARD ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, not optional. Add `scripts/tests/test-claude-refresh-matcher.sh` following the existing convention of the four tests already in `scripts/tests/`. It MUST assert, at minimum, all four of: (a) a process whose cgroup is under `/system.slice/` is NEVER selected; (b) a process that merely mentions `claude` somewhere in its argv, without being a Claude Code process, is NEVER selected; (c) an inhibitor whose held `tail --pid=<pid>` target is STILL ALIVE is NEVER selected; (d) the script's own subshells are NEVER self-selected. This is precisely the class of defect that silently reappears, which is why the assertions are named individually rather than left to the implementer's discretion.
2. Re-running the matcher in status mode on a live machine reports ZERO orphans when all Claude sessions are live, rather than the observed 11.
3. The reported reclaim figure matches the post-exclusion selection.
4. A real preview path exists for process cleanup and `commands/refresh.md`'s `--dry-run` description is true of the shipped behavior.
5. The timer/service and the installer-generated `ExecStart` are non-destructive by default, with `--force` as explicit opt-in.
6. No doc site claims a safety property the code does not implement.
7. `bash -n` clean on every edited script.

DELIVERABLE RULE: this task's deliverables outside `specs/**` must not cite task numbers.

artifacts.summary: Confirms all reported root causes at the line level, live-reproduces all false positives (including a new race-condition finding for the self-subshell case) on this machine read-only, and recommends a unifying single-snapshot ps -eo comm/cgroup/uid/liveness redesign plus a sourceable-main() test design closing all four required regression assertions.

completed_projects.completion_summary: Replaced /refresh's orphan-process matcher (two-stage ps-aux-regex-then-ancestor-walk) with a single atomic ps -eo snapshot and four independently-testable exclusion predicates, closing the false positives that misidentified a system OOM daemon, live sleep inhibitors, a memory-tracker service, and the script's own subshells as orphans (10/10 confirmed false positives on this machine, now 0). Shipped the required regression suite (RED-proven against the pre-fix script), made the hourly systemd timer non-destructive by default, fixed the pre-exclusion reclaim figure, added a genuine --dry-run preview path, and reconciled every doc site that claimed a safety property the code did not implement. All seven acceptance criteria verified PASS.

completed_projects.title: Make check_undeclared_scripts skip untracked build artifacts
completed_projects.description:
SOURCE-STORE RULE (binding): `.claude/**` is a GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE deploy artifact regenerated from the source store. ALL edits MUST target `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and NEVER `.claude/**`. Runtime invocations may still reference deployed `.claude/scripts/*` paths -- that is the CALL PATH, not the EDIT TARGET.

WHAT IS WRONG: `check_undeclared_scripts()` in `scripts/check-extension-docs.sh` enumerates candidate files with `find "$ext_path_norm/scripts" -type f` and exempts exactly one path shape, `deprecated/*`. Every other regular file found under an extension's `scripts/` tree is required to appear in that extension's `provides.scripts` manifest array or it is reported via `fail`. Because `find` walks the working tree rather than the git index, ANY untracked or gitignored file that happens to sit under `scripts/` -- build artifacts, caches, virtualenvs -- becomes a permanent, unfixable hard FAIL. The file cannot be declared in `provides.scripts` (it is not a deliverable and must never be deployed), and it cannot be removed permanently (it is regenerated by the next interpreter run).

OBSERVED LIVE (empirical, not code review): doc-lint reported two FAILs against files that are gitignored and were never tracked:
  - `agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/__pycache__/literature-decode-font-offset.cpython-313.pyc`
  - `agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/tests/__pycache__/generate-test-fixtures.cpython-313.pyc`
Both are CPython bytecode caches. Their presence makes `check-extension-docs.sh` exit non-zero unconditionally, so the doc-lint gate is permanently red and every consumer of that exit status inherits a standing failure.

THE FIX IS ALREADY CHOSEN AND ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE -- DO NOT REDESIGN IT. The sibling check `check_flat_category_orphans()` in this same script solved exactly this problem via its `_git_deployed_files()` helper, which enumerates with `git ls-files` instead of `find`, and carries this comment verbatim:

    # Enumeration method: git ls-files (not find), matching the research audit method -- naturally
    # excludes gitignored runtime artifacts (literature-pyenv/venv/, __pycache__/) without extra
    # path filtering, since they were never tracked.

WORK: apply that same already-chosen, already-justified enumeration method to `check_undeclared_scripts()`. Replace the `find`-based process substitution with a `git ls-files`-based one scoped to the extension's `scripts/` directory. Preserve every existing behavior of the check that is NOT about enumeration:
  - Matching remains by FULL RELATIVE PATH under `scripts/`, never by basename -- `provides.scripts` entries legitimately carry a path prefix (e.g. literature's `tests/generate-test-fixtures.py`).
  - All regular file types remain in scope, not just `*.sh` -- `provides.scripts` already holds `.sh`, `.py`, `.sql`, and dotfile entries (e.g. literature's `.zotero-title-sim.py`). Do not reintroduce a `*.sh` glob.
  - `deprecated/*` stays exempt; `tests/` stays NON-exempt (literature declares its `tests/*.py` and `tests/*.sh` entries deliberately).
  - The trailing-slash normalization (`ext_path_norm="${ext_path%/}"`) must survive. The caller's loop is `for ext_path in "$EXT_DIR"/*/`, so `ext_path` carries a trailing slash; left unstripped, the prefix-strip builds a double-slash prefix that matches nothing and degrades the check into reporting every script in every extension as undeclared. Re-verify this holds against whatever path form `git ls-files` returns, which is repo-root-relative and therefore NOT the same shape `find` returned -- the prefix-strip logic must be re-derived for the new form, not copied blindly.

DO NOT take the alternative of adding a `__pycache__/*` case to the existing `case` statement. That is a symptom patch: it fixes these two files and leaves the next gitignored artifact class (`.venv/`, `*.pyc` elsewhere, editor swap files, `node_modules/`) to reproduce the identical permanent-FAIL failure mode. The git-index enumeration is a class fix and is what the sibling check already committed to; divergent enumeration between two checks in one script is itself a defect worth closing.

VERIFICATION BAR (all must hold):
1. The two literature `__pycache__` FAILs no longer appear.
2. A genuinely undeclared BUT TRACKED script under an extension's `scripts/` is STILL caught. Add or verify a fixture proving this. This assertion is a HARD acceptance criterion, not optional -- the entire risk of this change is silently converting a working check into a no-op, and only a positive-detection fixture distinguishes "correctly ignores untracked artifacts" from "ignores everything".
3. A declared-and-tracked script produces no finding (no false positive regression).
4. `bash -n agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh` is clean.
5. `bash .claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh` exits 0.

DELIVERABLE RULE: this task's deliverables outside `specs/**` must not cite task numbers. Use durable anchors instead -- function names (`check_undeclared_scripts`, `check_flat_category_orphans`, `_git_deployed_files`), script names, and section headings.

Implementation summary covering all 4 phases: git ls-files enumeration replacement, header comment update, positive-detection fixture verification, and deploy propagation.

completed_projects.completion_summary: Replaced find-based enumeration in check_undeclared_scripts() with git ls-files, re-derived the REPO_ROOT-relative prefix-strip and existence guard, updated the header comment, empirically verified via a positive-detection fixture that tracked-but-undeclared scripts are still caught (HARD gate passed), and propagated the fix through the deploy path -- the two literature __pycache__ FAILs are gone and the doc-lint gate exits 0.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a `git-commit-scoped.sh`-style targeted commit against a task directory whose auto-injected ephemeral excludes include a currently-existing gitignored subdirectory (e.g. specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/.lock/ held by an active task-lock), `git add <dir>/ :(exclude)<dir>/.lock/` used to fail with 'paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files' and exit 1 -- git treats an exclude pathspec that names an already-gitignored path as an explicit mention, which it refuses, even though `git add <dir>/` alone (recursing without any exclude pathspec) silently skips the same ignored subdirectory with exit 0. This is now FIXED at the source: git-commit-scoped.sh injects each candidate exclude entry only when `git check-ignore -q` reports it is NOT already covered by .gitignore, so a covered path (the normal case in this repo) is never named in an exclude pathspec and cannot trigger the abort. The trigger was the `:(exclude)` entry naming a gitignored path, never a trailing slash on the positive pathspec entry -- any record claiming a trailing-slash omission avoids the abort is false. The previously-recorded workaround (stage the task directory's specific subpaths individually instead of the whole directory glob) is superseded by the shipped fix and should not be used.

To empirically verify a change to a doc-lint/enumeration check does not silently degrade into a no-op, use a three-property test: (1) diff the pre-change vs post-change output and confirm the delta is EXACTLY the expected removed findings, (2) confirm the finding count for a clean tree is zero (no regression), and (3) build a positive-detection fixture (e.g. `git add -N` an intentionally-noncompliant file) and confirm the check still reports it, then clean up and re-verify output matches baseline. This three-property pattern (skip untracked / no false positives / still catches violations) is reusable for any enumeration-method change (find -> git ls-files, glob -> index-driven, etc.).
